paragraphs: Frontline Wildfire Defense sells exterior sprinkler systems and companion software that defend homes and businesses against wildfire. The company describes its mission as providing faster, safer and more precise ways to protect homes, families, businesses and communities from wildfire.

The second-generation defense system is tied to fire tracking software and turns on automatically when fire comes within seven miles of a home. Once running, it saturates the property with water and biodegradable firefighting foam to create conditions the company calls too wet to burn. A commercial version is aimed at businesses, campuses and critical infrastructure, meant to cut risk before a fire reaches the property. A companion app carries wildfire alerts, maps, fire danger indexes, emergency contact groups and evacuation checklists.

Homeowners, businesses and new housing developments are the audience, and the company says its system will safeguard 151 homes at a Woodside Homes community. Installation is handled by licensed contractors in each state rather than by the company itself. Financing options, including zero-down wildfire protection, are offered to buyers. The company points to embers as the central danger, saying they cause up to 90% of structure loss during a wildfire.
